lesson.title: Make two cells

steps.headline: Mitosis shares a cell's copied chromosomes equally between two new nuclei.

lead.text: Before dividing, a cell copies its DNA. In mitosis the sister chromatids of every chromosome are pulled apart, and one copy goes to each new nucleus.
Cytokinesis then splits the cell. The results are two daughter cells.
Think of the worksheet. Each student got a full set. A daughter cell needs a full set of chromosomes too.

reveal.text: You predicted that each daughter keeps the parent's number. Sister chromatids separate equally, so the chromosome number does not change.

steps.headline: A cell has 3 chromosomes before replication. How many DNA molecules does it have afterwards?

workedSteps.text: Replication copies every chromosome. Each one now has two sister chromatids.
Each chromatid is one DNA molecule.
Count two molecules for each chromosome.

steps.headline: A cell has 6 chromosomes before replication. How many DNA molecules does it have afterwards?

workedSteps.text: Each chromosome is copied, so it has two chromatids.
Count two DNA molecules for each of the six chromosomes.

steps.headline: Cells divide when the body needs more of them. Division is regulated.

lead.text: Cells divide for growth, repair and reproduction. Signals and conditions switch division on and off, so a tissue makes only the cells it needs.
In an ideal case every cell divides once in each round, so every cell becomes two.

reveal.text: Three rounds gave three doublings. Real tissues grow more slowly, because only some cells divide in each round.

lead.text: In a real tissue, regulation decides which cells divide. Suppose that in one round, only half of the cells do.

reveal.text: Only the dividing cells added to the total, so the tissue grew by less than a doubling. That is regulation at work.

lesson.orientation: Track chromosomes through mitotic division and connect division to growth and repair.
lesson.nextAction: Try the next idea, then return for a fresh problem after a delay.

blocks.text: A worksheet has 5 pages. A teacher photocopies the whole set once.
The original set goes to one student and the copy goes to another.

intro.promise: By the end you'll follow chromosomes through mitosis and count cells as a tissue grows.
intro.whyItMatters: It is how a single fertilised egg becomes a body, and how a cut heals.

recap.keyIdea: Mitosis copies the DNA and then shares it, so each daughter cell keeps the parent's chromosome number. Regulation decides which cells divide.

blocks.text: You followed 4 chromosomes into each daughter cell and counted DNA molecules after replication.
You also counted cells through ideal doublings and through a tissue where only some cells divide.

recap.nextHook: Sex cells need only half the chromosomes. How does a cell halve a chromosome set?

questions.prompt: Name the nuclear division process used in ordinary tissue growth and repair.
hints: It keeps the starting chromosome number.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Mitosis distributes copied chromosomes to daughter nuclei during regulated growth and repair.

questions.onCorrect: Mitosis. It shares copied chromosomes so each daughter nucleus gets a full set.

misconceptions.feedback: Meiosis makes sex cells and halves the chromosome number. Growth needs the full number kept.

questions.prompt: A cell has 6 chromosomes before replication. How many DNA molecules does it have after replication but before mitosis?
hints: Replication copies the DNA.
Each of the six chromosomes now has two chromatids.
Count the two DNA molecules in every replicated chromosome.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Six replicated chromosomes have two chromatids each: 12 DNA molecules.

questions.onCorrect: 12. Every chromosome is copied, so it holds two DNA molecules.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the number of chromosomes. Each one now holds two DNA molecules.
That doubles twice. Replication copies each chromosome only once.

questions.prompt: A cell starts with 4 chromosomes and completes normal mitosis and cytokinesis. How many chromosomes are in each daughter cell?
hints: Think about the worksheet: each student got a full set.
Sister chromatids are separated equally.
Each daughter gets the same number the parent started with.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Each daughter retains the original four chromosomes.

questions.onCorrect: 4. Mitosis gives each daughter a full set, so the chromosome number stays the same.

misconceptions.feedback: Mitosis does not halve the number. Each daughter gets a full set.
That counts the chromatids before they separate. Each daughter gets one copy of each chromosome.

questions.prompt: One cell completes three ideal rounds of division, with every descendant dividing each round. How many cells result?
hints: Double once for each round.
After two rounds there are four cells.
Double the count a third time.
questions.onCorrect: 8. Each round doubles the number of cells, so three rounds make three doublings.

misconceptions.feedback: That adds two for each round. Each round doubles the count instead.
That counts the rounds. The question asks for the number of cells.

questions.prompt: Name the two joined copies of a replicated chromosome that separate during mitosis.
hints: Track the two copies made by DNA replication.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Sister chromatids separate and become daughter chromosomes.

questions.onCorrect: Sister chromatids. They separate so each daughter nucleus gets one copy.

misconceptions.feedback: Homologous chromosomes are separate chromosomes from two parents. The joined copies came from one.

questions.prompt: Does a normal body cell divide only because it is about to die?
hints: Separate regulated division from cell death.

acceptedIdeas: No, division is regulated for growth, repair and other needs
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Cell-cycle regulation responds to conditions and signals; imminent death is not the general cause.

choices.label: Yes, that is the defining trigger
No, division is regulated for growth, repair and other needs
Yes, and the DNA need not be copied

questions.onCorrect: No. Division is regulated and happens when the body needs new cells.

misconceptions.feedback: Cells divide when growth or repair needs them to. Dying is not the trigger.
DNA is always copied first. Without a copy, a daughter would lack half its instructions.

questions.prompt: After replication, a cell has 10 DNA molecules. How many chromosomes does it have?
hints: How many DNA molecules does one replicated chromosome hold?
Each replicated chromosome has two chromatids.
Share the DNA molecules out two to a chromosome.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Each chromosome now holds two DNA molecules, so 10 ÷ 2 = 5 chromosomes.

questions.onCorrect: 5. Two DNA molecules per replicated chromosome, so halve the count of DNA molecules.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the number of DNA molecules. Two of them make up each chromosome.
Replication has already happened. Work back from the DNA molecules.

questions.prompt: One cell completes four ideal rounds of division, with every descendant dividing each round. How many cells result?
hints: Double once for each round.
Three rounds give eight cells.
Double the count once more.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the count after three rounds. There is one more.
That counts the rounds. Each round doubles the cell count.

questions.prompt: How many pages does each student receive?
hints: Each student gets a whole set, not part of one.
How many pages are in one set?
The copy is as long as the original.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Each student gets one complete set, which has 5 pages.

questions.onCorrect: 5. Each side gets a full set. Dividing cells copy their chromosomes before sharing them out.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the total number of pages. Each student gets one set only.
That counts the students. The question asks about pages.

questions.prompt: Why does each sister chromatid count as one DNA molecule?
hints: What did replication copy?

acceptedIdeas: It is one copy of the chromosome's DNA
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Each chromatid is one complete copy of the chromosome's DNA molecule.

choices.label: It is one copy of the chromosome's DNA
It is half a DNA molecule
It is a protein, not DNA

questions.onCorrect: Each chromatid is one complete copy. Two chromatids mean two DNA molecules.

misconceptions.feedback: Replication makes complete copies, not halves.
Chromatids are made of DNA with its proteins. The DNA is what is counted.

questions.prompt: A tissue has 8 cells. In one round only half of them divide, and each of those becomes two cells. How many cells are there after that round?
hints: How many cells divide?
Each dividing cell becomes two, a gain of one.
Add the gain to the cells you started with.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Four cells divide into eight, and four do not: 8 + 4 = 12 cells.

questions.onCorrect: 12. Only the dividing cells add to the total, so regulated tissue grows more slowly than ideal doubling.

misconceptions.feedback: That doubles all the cells. Only half of them divide here.
That is the starting count. The dividing cells add to it.
